title: K8s Admission with Gatekeeper
subtitle: ConstraintTemplates, Constraints, and deny
content:
🚪 Policy at the Cluster Door

Requires: basic Pod/YAML familiarity (reading spec.containers). No cluster needed — review the manifests statically.

Admission control is authorization for the orchestrator: every create/update to the API server passes Gatekeeper's webhook before etcd. Two objects: a ConstraintTemplate (the Rego rule, written once) and Constraints (instances with parameters and match scope, written per team). Verified against Gatekeeper docs and library patterns:

ConstraintTemplate: CRD + all-containers violation (verified pattern) 
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs Gatekeeper docs (ConstraintTemplate + library)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sallowedrepos
spec:
  # Mandatory: the CRD backing Constraint instances (apply fails without it)
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAllowedRepos
      validation:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sallowedrepos
        # Library pattern: ALL container lists, or init/ephemeral bypass you
        all_containers[c] { c := input.review.object.spec.containers[_] }
        all_containers[c] { c := input.review.object.spec.initContainers[_] }
        all_containers[c] { c := input.review.object.spec.ephemeralContainers[_] }
        violation[{"msg": msg}] if {
          not startswith(all_containers[_].image, "corp-registry.example.com/")
          msg := sprintf("image %v is not from the allowlisted registry", [all_containers[_].image])
        }
# Last verified: 2026-09 vs Gatekeeper docs (ConstraintTemplate + library) apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1 kind: ConstraintTemplate metadata: name: k8sallowedrepos spec: # Mandatory: the CRD backing Constraint instances (apply fails without it) crd: spec: names: kind: K8sAllowedRepos validation: openAPIV3Schema: type: object targets: - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh rego: | package k8sallowedrepos # Library pattern: ALL container lists, or init/ephemeral bypass you all_containers[c] { c := input.review.object.spec.containers[_] } all_containers[c] { c := input.review.object.spec.initContainers[_] } all_containers[c] { c := input.review.object.spec.ephemeralContainers[_] } violation[{"msg": msg}] if { not startswith(all_containers[_].image, "corp-registry.example.com/") msg := sprintf("image %v is not from the allowlisted registry", [all_containers[_].image]) }
Constraint: scope + enforcement action 
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sAllowedRepos
metadata:
  name: prod-allowlist
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny        # deny | dryrun | warn
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    excludedNamespaces: [kube-system, gatekeeper-system]
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1 kind: K8sAllowedRepos metadata: name: prod-allowlist spec: enforcementAction: deny # deny | dryrun | warn match: kinds: - apiGroups: [""] kinds: ["Pod"] excludedNamespaces: [kube-system, gatekeeper-system]

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • Containers AND initContainers AND ephemeralContainers: the library pattern checks all three. Guarding only spec.containers is a bypass with a YAML edit.
  • Start with dryrun: new constraints audit first (violations logged, nothing blocked), then flip to deny. Big-bang deny on a brownfield cluster is a self-inflicted outage.
  • exemptImages has no per-namespace scoping: docs-verified — different namespaces needing different exemptions require separate constraints, not one clever parameter.
  • Mutation exists (Assign/AssignImage): defaulting digests and labels is powerful — and a second write path to review with the same rigor as deny rules.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Compare sidecar vs gateway vs admission: who decides, when, with what blast radius. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: What is the split between ConstraintTemplate and Constraint?

options.text: Template holds the Rego rule once; Constraints instantiate it with parameters and match scope
Constraints hold Rego, Templates hold YAML

questions.explanation: Write the logic once, scope it per team. Templates are code; Constraints are configuration.

questions.question: A Pod runs a privileged initContainer while containers are clean. A containers-only image policy verdict?

options.text: Misses it — initContainers (and ephemeralContainers) need the same checks
The Pod is rejected for other reasons

questions.explanation: The library pattern enumerates all three container lists. Partial coverage is a documented bypass.

questions.question: Rolling a new image-allowlist onto a brownfield cluster. First enforcementAction?

options.text: dryrun — audit violations first, flip to deny after triage

questions.explanation: Unknown estate plus instant deny equals outage. Dry-run measures the blast radius before you create it.

questions.question: Two namespaces need different image exemptions. Approach?

options.text: Separate Constraints — exemptImages has no per-namespace scoping
One Constraint with a clever exemptImages map

questions.explanation: Docs-verified limitation. Fighting it with custom Rego forks you from the maintained library.

questions.question: Where does admission control sit in the request path?

options.text: Between API-server receipt and etcd persist — every create/update passes the webhook
After the Pod is already running

questions.explanation: Admission is deploy-time authorization for the orchestrator. Runtime needs its own controls.

questions.question: AssignImage pins nginx to a digest via mutation. Review posture?

options.text: Same rigor as deny rules — mutation is a second write path into every Pod

questions.explanation: Anything that rewrites workloads is privileged. Mutation policies get tests, review, and dry-run too.

questions.question: excludedNamespaces lists kube-system and gatekeeper-system. Why?

options.text: So policy infrastructure itself is never blocked by its own rules
Those namespaces are insecure by design

questions.explanation: Self-lockout is the classic admission failure. The controller that enforces policy must stay schedulable.

questions.question: A workload violates a dryrun constraint. What happens to the deploy?

options.text: It proceeds; the violation is logged for triage

questions.explanation: Dry-run is measurement mode. The log it produces is the evidence base for flipping to deny.
